title: Zoetis Raises 2026 EPS Forecast to $6.25-$6.35 as Pet Care Demand Stays Soft
text:
Zoetis Raises 2026 EPS Forecast to $6.25-$6.35 as Pet Care Demand Stays Soft — BigGo Finance Ask AI Real-time News Market Earnings Call Event Calendar Watchlist Podcast Market Influencers Earnings Call Event Calendar Watchlist Podcast Market Influencers More Ask AI Real-time News Watchlist Holdings Market Earnings Call Event Calendar Podcast Market Influencers Zoetis Raises 2026 EPS Forecast to $6.25-$6.35 as Pet Care Demand Stays Soft
 Add preferred source Zoetis raised its 2026 adjusted earnings guidance to $6.25-$6.35 per share and narrowed its revenue forecast to $9.22 billion-$9.32 billion after third-quarter results beat estimates. Adjusted EPS of $1.75 topped the $1.51 consensus, while revenue slipped 1% to $2.391 billion. U.S. sales fell 6% on an 8% decline in companion animal revenue, with dermatology down 16% amid generic and competitive pressure. Livestock grew 7% and diagnostics rose 13%. Management said it will plan conservatively for 2027, assuming no improvement in the pet care market. Key Elements 
 Zoetis Inc. Kristin Peck James Saccaro Apoquel Cytopoint Simparica Convenia Cerenia Librela Solensia Companion Animal Diagnostics Livestock Zoetis Inc. (NYSE:ZTS) lifted its full-year profit outlook on Thursday even as the animal health company reported a slight decline in third-quarter revenue, with its top executive describing results as consistent with internal expectations amid a cautious pet care market.
 The Parsippany, New Jersey-based company now expects 2026 adjusted earnings of $6.25 to $6.35 per share, up from a prior range of $6.15 to $6.25. It narrowed its sales forecast to $9.22 billion to $9.32 billion from $9.12 billion to $9.32 billion, implying an organic operational decline of 1% to 2%.
 Third-quarter adjusted earnings came in at $1.75 per share, ahead of the $1.51 consensus. Revenue fell 1% to $2.391 billion on both a reported and organic operational basis, but still cleared the roughly $2.3 billion analysts had projected. Adjusted net income was $720 million, down 7% on an organic operational basis.
 "Our third-quarter performance was in line with our expectations. Continued pressure in Companion Animal was partially offset by growth in Livestock and Diagnostics, reflecting the breadth of our portfolio," Chief Executive Kristin Peck said in a statement.
 The split between the company's two main businesses told the story of the quarter. U.S. revenue fell 6% to $1.2 billion, dragged down by an 8% drop in companion animal sales, while livestock revenue rose 5% on strength in cattle, swine and poultry. Internationally, sales grew 4% to $1.1 billion, helped by an 8% increase in livestock.
 Companion animal revenue globally declined 5% to $1.6 billion. The dermatology franchise was the weakest link, falling 16% to $396 million, with U.S. sales down 13% to $266 million as the company lost share on Apoquel and faced competitive pressure from new injectable treatments. Cytopoint also slipped as canine veterinary visits fell about 5% and itch-related visits dropped roughly 3%.
 Generic competition against Convenia and Cerenia continued to weigh on results, though the pace of volume declines eased to the lowest level since the copycat products entered the market in the first quarter. The Simparica franchise grew 1% to $358 million globally, with international sales up 10% on Simparica Trio momentum in Europe and Latin America, offsetting a 2% decline in the U.S.
 Segment Q3 Revenue Change (Organic Operational) 
 U.S. $1.2 billion -6% 
 International $1.1 billion +4% 
 Companion Animal (global) $1.6 billion -5% 
 Livestock (global) $797 million +7% 
 Key Dermatology (global) $396 million -16% 
 Simparica (global) $358 million +1% 
 Companion Animal Diagnostics $122 million +13% 
 Note: Changes are on a reported and organic operational basis as disclosed by the company.
 On a call with analysts, Chief Financial Officer James Saccaro pointed to a mix of headwinds. "Our diverse portfolio and disciplined commercial execution continue to help us navigate an operating environment shaped by competitive pressure in our key Companion Animal franchises, softer clinic visits, and ongoing affordability headwinds for pet owners," he said.
 The company said U.S. clinic visits are down 3% year to date across categories, reflecting high housing costs that are curbing pet adoption, fewer dogs entering households and owners making trade-offs on care. Management also noted that veterinary service costs have climbed about 50% since 2022, well ahead of general inflation, making pet owners more value-conscious.
 Zoetis has responded with gross-to-net promotional spending rather than list-price cuts, and it said the effort slowed U.S. dermatology share loss to about 4 percentage points in the third quarter from roughly 7 points in the second. It also held its 22.5% U.S. share in Simparica Trio.
 Looking ahead, Saccaro said the company will budget conservatively for 2027 and is not assuming any improvement in the macro environment, pet owner spending or competitive dynamics. New product launches, including a long-acting version of Cytopoint expected to win U.S. approval in the fourth quarter and Simparica Duo by year-end, are expected to contribute only modestly next year before building into 2028.
 The cautious tone underscores the pressure on a business long viewed as a steady grower. Shares rose about 2% in premarket trading following the release, according to Investing.com.
 For investors, the key question is whether the promotional defense can hold share until the pet care cycle turns. Zoetis is betting that a broad portfolio, cost discipline and a pipeline spanning renal disease, oncology, cardiology and obesity will carry it through. Adjusted operating expenses were flat at $749 million, with selling, general and administrative costs and research spending each unchanged as cost programs offset higher data and digital investment.
 The company also recorded a $78 million impairment charge on previously acquired in-process research and development assets, reflecting revised development and commercial assumptions.
